name: Meter corridor
description: A corridor whose two walls are racked floor to ceiling with moving-coil VU meters, flown down at rack height. The chassis is marched and repeated by domain folding, so one distance evaluation covers the whole wall; the printed scales, red zones, peak lamps and tapered needles are drawn in each panel's own coordinates wherever the ray lands, so they take real perspective and the glass over them reflects the room hard at grazing angles. Each rack is detuned slightly from its neighbours, so the wall ripples rather than moving as one dial. The analysis is mono, so the two meters on a panel read the low and the high half of the spectrum rather than a left and a right that do not exist.

left.description: Deflection of the left (or upper) needle, 0 to 1 across the scale. The default is a bass-weighted mix with a little onset on top, which is the overshoot a real needle has on a transient.

right.description: Deflection of the right (or lower) needle.

leftPeak.description: What the left peak lamp watches. Use the peak-hold sources here, not the bands: the lamp is meant to catch a transient the needle is too slow to show.

tint.description: Pulls the cream card, amber lamp and red zone toward the project palette. 0 leaves the classic hi-fi colours; 1 puts the whole panel in the video's colour world and loses most of what makes it read as a VU meter.

glow.description: Backlight behind the cards, and the haze the lit wells throw into the corridor in front of them.

travel.description: How fast the camera flies down the corridor. Negative runs it backwards; 0 holds still between two walls of meters.

lean.description: How far the racks lean in and out along the corridor. 0 gives two flat walls, which reads as a diagram; a little of it makes the wall breathe.
